description: Recommends transferring $766,300 to the Special Events Reserve.
Recommends limiting special event applications for 2026 and 2027.
Administration to report on future event funding by 2028.

chips.text: City Manager Jorgensen strongly disagreed with Discover Saskatoon's claims about the city's agility.
Discover Saskatoon advocated for strategic event funding and partnership.
Mayor Block questioned if the city could remain agile for quick event decisions.
Discover Saskatoon highlighted that public disclosure of bids weakens Saskatoon's competitiveness.
Administration will report on how other cities structure special event funding programs.

segments.title: Administration Presentation on Funding Options
segments.takeaway: Administration presented three funding options for special events, recommending option one for short-term stability and temporary program changes for fairness and fiscal responsibility.

segments.title: Public Speaker: Discover Saskatoon
segments.takeaway: Discover Saskatoon's CEO spoke, supporting stabilization but urging a strategic approach that differentiates events, protects competitiveness, and includes Discover Saskatoon as a partner.

segments.title: Questions for Discover Saskatoon
segments.takeaway: Councillor Parker questioned Discover Saskatoon about their proposed different funding streams and the need for a non-one-size-fits-all policy for events.

segments.title: Questions for Administration on Funding Options and Agility
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block questioned administration on the rebalancing of reserves, the agility of the funding process for major events, and the impact of public disclosure on competitive bids.

segments.title: Questions for Administration on Adjudication and Intake Changes
segments.takeaway: Councillor Parker questioned administration on the adjudication criteria, the equitable distribution of funds, and the rationale behind reducing the number of annual funding intakes.

segments.title: Questions for Administration on Short-Term vs. Long-Term Intake Strategy
segments.takeaway: Councillor Timon inquired about the temporary nature of the single intake process and whether future reports would propose options for returning to multiple intakes based on funding levels.

segments.title: Questions for Administration on Program Subscription and Event Planning
segments.takeaway: Chair Keller asked administration about historical program subscription, the approval process for events, and the feasibility of event planners adapting to a single annual intake.

segments.title: Council Comments on Recommendations
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block commented on the importance of a healthy special event reserve and signaled an upcoming motion to better understand the city's competitiveness compared to other municipalities.

segments.title: Vote on Main Recommendations
segments.takeaway: The committee voted to approve the administration's main recommendations regarding the funding for special events.

segments.title: Motion Arising: Report on Comparator Municipalities
segments.takeaway: Mayor Block moved a motion for administration to report back on how comparator municipalities structure their special event funding programs and align with economic development objectives.

segments.title: Vote on Motion Arising
segments.takeaway: The committee voted unanimously to approve the motion for administration to report on special event funding structures in comparator municipalities.

Committee recommends developing a city land policy for affordable housing.
Policy would guide land disposition and acquisition processes.
Policy would ensure long-term affordability for projects.

chips.text: Chair emphasized importance of long-term affordability in the new policy.
New policy replaces current ad hoc approach to city land for housing.
No conclusive research guides long-term affordable housing expiry dates.
Métis Nation–Saskatchewan strongly supports the proposed land policy.
Policy would prioritize land sales to Indigenous-led developers.
Administration will develop the policy and bring it back for approval.

speakers.name: Lesley Anderson
speakers.summary: Lesley Anderson, Director of Planning and Development presented the report and responded to questions of the Committee related to the policy, long term affordability and community impact.
said: Policy provides a deliberate, long-term approach to securing affordable housing land.
It reduces upfront land costs and strengthens city's funding position.
Key elements include inventory, council approval, Indigenous priority, and development-ready sites.

description: Committee recommends RFP for Farmer's Market Building management.
RFP includes 120 Sonnenschein Way as optional component.
Prioritize proposals enhancing market success and community benefit.

chips.text: Administration clarified structured incubator programming ceased some time ago.
Tenants and vendors at Gather Local Market and 120 Sonnenschein Way.
Tenants of 120 Sonnenschein Way were not consulted for the report.
Delegates expressed strong support for the market's community and incubation services.
Negotiations underway with 57 black-owned startup businesses for market participation.

segments.title: Staff Presentation on Gather Local Market and Ideas Inc. Operations
segments.takeaway: Administration provided an update on the operations of Gather Local Market and Ideas Inc., detailing their financial struggles, lease surrenders, and the city's interim management of both facilities.

segments.title: Public Comments - Karen Colbison
segments.takeaway: Karen Colbison, a tenant at Ideas Inc., spoke about the strong sense of community and support the space fostered for local businesses, praising administration's handling of the transition.

segments.title: Public Comments - Notion Ellie
segments.takeaway: Notion Ellie, a contractor for Gather Local Market, highlighted the market's transformation into a vibrant community hub and expressed vendor concerns about the impact of a new operator.

segments.title: Public Comments - Braden Goldstein
segments.takeaway: Braden Goldstein spoke on behalf of Ideas Inc. tenants, emphasizing the critical role of small business incubation services and the lack of tenant consultation in the report.

segments.title: Questions for Administration
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned administration about the RFP process, the definition of incubation services, the financial viability of the buildings, and the timeline for securing a new operator.
